title: What Are the Best AI Penetration Testing Tools in Japan? [October 2026]
summary: Compare the best AI penetration testing tools in Japan for 2026: MindFort, XBOW, Pentera, Horizon3.ai, RunSybil, PentAGI, GMO Ierae, and NRI Secure.
body_markdown:
This guide explains why Japanese companies are under pressure to run more penetration tests and vulnerability assessments in 2026. It compares six AI pentesting tools with two leading Japanese security firms. It also covers the rules Japanese buyers need to meet.


## Why are Japanese companies under pressure to pentest now?


LDP cyber chief Masaaki Taira said on October 9 that the situation "could even be called an emergency in cyberspace,"[Asahi reported ↗](https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/33e384890f26e79f49b0f92ed51bf546c29b9ebd) . The same day, the[National Cybersecurity Office ↗](https://www.cyber.go.jp/pdf/press/taiou.pdf) told companies to assume they could be attacked at any time. It asked them to run vulnerability assessments on a regular schedule. The warnings followed a wave of breaches:


- [Times Car ↗](https://atmarkit.itmedia.co.jp/ait/articles/2609/30/news038.html) disclosed about 6.6 million affected accounts on September 28.
- [Ransomware hit IDC Frontier ↗](https://www.watch.impress.co.jp/docs/news/2146693.html) on October 7 and took cloud services offline for 495 companies and local governments.
- [JR East ↗](https://www.jreast.co.jp/press/2026/20261009_ho02.pdf) warned that up to 1.67 million Eki-net email addresses may have leaked through that attack.
- [BOOKOFF and the Yakiniku King app ↗](https://www.itmedia.co.jp/news/article/2610/09/2000002161/) reported millions of member records at risk.


## What changes with Japan's new security rating and Active Cyber Defense law?


METI's[supply chain security rating (SCS) ↗](https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/netsecurity/scs.html) opens for 3-star and 4-star applications around early 2027. A[4-star rating ↗](https://www.meti.go.jp/policy/netsecurity/docs/scs/scs_2.pdf) includes a technical vulnerability test of internet-facing VPNs and routers. It also expects critical and high vulnerabilities fixed within 14 days. Since October 1, 2026, the[Active Cyber Defense law ↗](https://atmarkit.itmedia.co.jp/ait/articles/2610/03/news001.html) has also required critical infrastructure operators to report incidents and vulnerabilities.

### 1. What is MindFort best for?


MindFort deploys autonomous AI agents that run black-box and white-box tests on your apps continuously. It's the fastest tool on this list to get started: run a test today and get findings in hours without a sales call. Every finding ships with proof of exploit, a pull request with a validated fix, and a retest. MindFort is a newer company with less funding than XBOW or Pentera.


### 2. What is XBOW best for?


XBOW runs autonomous pentests against[web applications and their APIs ↗](https://docs.xbow.com/console/reference/asset-types) . Targets must be reachable from the public internet. It offers a[Tokyo data region ↗](https://docs.xbow.com/console/reference/data-residency/) in private preview, though AI model prompts may still be processed outside Japan. Its[AWS Marketplace listing ↗](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-aj7ajvgepa5mm) starts at $50,000 for 12 months, and our[MindFort vs XBOW](https://www.mindfort.ai/compare/mindfort-vs-xbow) comparison goes deeper.


### 3. What is Pentera best for?


Pentera validates security controls across networks, Active Directory, and cloud. It sells in Japan through reseller[Techmatrix ↗](https://www.techmatrix.co.jp/nc/news/20250326-pentera-pressrelease.html) . Its[AI web app pentesting ↗](https://pentera.io/press-release/pentera-ai-web-app-pentesting/) is still in beta for selected customers. Its[AWS Marketplace listing ↗](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-56i5cowyjxcxm) is $120,000 for 12 months, and our[MindFort vs Pentera](https://www.mindfort.ai/compare/mindfort-vs-pentera) comparison goes deeper.


### 4. What is Horizon3.ai NodeZero best for?


NodeZero runs autonomous pentests against networks, Active Directory, and cloud. Tokyo-based[Parongo became a NodeZero reseller ↗](https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000013.000047170.html) in June 2026. Its[WebApp module launched in July 2026 ↗](https://horizon3.ai/news/press-release/nodezero-webapp-launch/) , so web testing is newer than its network core.[AWS Marketplace pricing ↗](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-l4tou5vhpvarm) starts at $25,000 a year for 500 assets, and our[MindFort vs Horizon3.ai](https://www.mindfort.ai/compare/mindfort-vs-horizon3) comparison goes deeper.


### 5. What is RunSybil best for?


RunSybil's agent[tests web and API attack surfaces ↗](https://www.runsybil.com/platform) in black-box, grey-box, or white-box mode. It[raised $40M led by Khosla Ventures ↗](https://www.runsybil.com/post/runsybil-raises-40m-to-build-the-ai-native-platform-for-offensive-security) in March 2026. Its[trust center ↗](https://trust.runsybil.com/) lists SOC 2 Type 2 and no hosting region. We found no partners or offices in Japan, and our[MindFort vs RunSybil](https://www.mindfort.ai/compare/mindfort-vs-runsybil) comparison goes deeper.


### 6. What is PentAGI best for?


[PentAGI ↗](https://github.com/vxcontrol/pentagi) is a free, MIT-licensed multi-agent system that you host yourself. It runs tools like nmap, Metasploit, and sqlmap inside an isolated Docker sandbox. It can use local models, so test data can stay on servers in Japan. You run and patch it yourself with community support only.


## How do AI tools compare with GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae and NRI Secure?


Japan's top human-led firms are strong, and both now add AI to their services. They fit one-off needs like TLPT, a pre-launch assessment, or a 4-star technical verification. Both appear on the[IPA's registered pentest service list ↗](https://www.ipa.go.jp/security/ug65p90000019fc0-att/20261009_6.pdf) . They cost more per test and run on a fixed schedule.


### What does GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae offer?


GMO's group has[more than 1,100 people working in security ↗](https://group.gmo/en/news/article/844) . Its Blue Water team[won the DEF CON 34 CTF ↗](https://scan.netsecurity.ne.jp/article/2026/08/17/55937.html) in August 2026. In July 2026 it launched an[AI White Hacker penetration test ↗](https://scan.netsecurity.ne.jp/article/2026/08/07/55882.html) that pairs AI with human testers. Pricing is quoted per engagement.


### What does NRI Secure offer?


NRI Secure launched a[frontier AI vulnerability assessment ↗](https://www.nri.com/jp/news/newsrelease/20260623_1.html) in June 2026. In September 2026 it[moved its AI assessments onto Amazon Bedrock in Tokyo and Osaka ↗](https://www.nri.com/jp/news/info/20260917_1.html) to keep data in Japan. Like GMO, it quotes each engagement separately.


## How should a Japanese company choose an AI pentesting tool?


Start with what you need to test and how often. Then check each vendor against this list:


- **Scope:** web apps, APIs, internal networks, cloud, or source code
- **Proof:** a working exploit for every finding
- **Fixes:** patch pull requests and automatic retests
- **Evidence:** reports and an attestation letter for auditors and regulators
- **Data residency:** where test data and LLM calls go
- **Cost:** a monthly price you can compare with a per-engagement quote

## FAQ


### Did the Japanese government declare a cyber emergency?


Not formally. On October 9, 2026, LDP cyber chief Masaaki Taira said the situation could be called an emergency in cyberspace. The National Cybersecurity Office issued an alert the same day. Nine agencies, including the FSA and METI, had published related alerts by October 14.


### Is penetration testing required by law in Japan?


Not for most companies. The National Cybersecurity Office now urges companies to run vulnerability assessments on a regular schedule. The new 4-star supply chain rating will also include a technical vulnerability test.


### What does APPI require after a breach?


Companies must report qualifying leaks to the Personal Information Protection Commission. A preliminary report is due within 3 to 5 days. A final report is due within 30 days, or 60 days if the leak may be malicious.
